input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The missing or invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify emits warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so the failure no longer stops the request.
- failure path: A user passes verify="/etc/ssl/missing.pem" (or certifi returns an empty path); only a warning is emitted and execution continues to configure the connection with a nonexistent bundle, producing a later, misleading SSL or TypeError at connect time instead of the clear OSError.

Reviewer finding
- description: The missing-CA-bundle check now emits a warning instead of raising OSError, so a nonexistent verify path or certifi path no longer fails fast with the intended clear error.
- rationale: Trigger: a caller passes verify='/nonexistent/ca.pem' (or the bundle path is missing). Before, cert_loc failed os.path.exists and OSError was raised with a clear message. Now warnings.warn is called and execution continues with a bad path, so the failure surfaces later from the TLS layer with a less clear error, or the warning is silently ignored. The commit title only announces removing the extraction call, not changing this error path to a warning, so the change is not covered by the stated intent.
critique: The finding says the missing CA bundle path check now calls warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so execution continues with a bad path and fails later with a less clear TLS-layer error. That is the same faulty operation and the same consequence as the label.
